A.explanation: Initial kinetic energy $0.5 \times 0.150 \times 2.0^2 = 0.30 \text{ J}$ divided by $30 \text{ m}$ gives $0.010 \text{ N}$.

B.explanation: This is double the correct value and results from omitting the $0.5$ in $E_k = 0.5mv^2$.

C.explanation: This uses mass in grams as $150$ instead of $0.150 \text{ kg}$, giving a kinetic energy 1000 times too large before dividing by distance.

hints: Notice the puck starts with $2.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and stops after $30 \text{ m}$, so its initial kinetic energy is completely removed by friction.
Connect energy loss to work done: work by a constant force is $W = Fd$, here with $d = 30 \text{ m}$ opposite to motion.
First convert $150 \text{ g}$ to $0.150 \text{ kg}$, calculate $0.5mv^2$, then divide that energy by $30 \text{ m}$ to get $F$ in newtons.
walkthrough: Convert the mass to SI units: $m = 150 \text{ g} = 0.150 \text{ kg}$, with $u = 2.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 0$ and stopping distance $d = 30 \text{ m}$.
State the energy principle: the work done by the average frictional force equals the loss of kinetic energy, so $F \times d = 0.5mu^2 - 0$.
Calculate the initial kinetic energy: $E_k = 0.5 \times 0.150 \times (2.0)^2 = 0.5 \times 0.150 \times 4.0 = 0.30 \text{ J}$.
Evaluate with units: $F = 0.010 \text{ N}$, which opposes the $30 \text{ m}$ slide. This is option A.
